subjects.heroTitle: Ten subjects designed for the Quebec curriculum
subjects.heroSubtitle: From primary to secondary, continuous progression and clear objectives for every year.

mathematiques.title: Mathematics
mathematiques.shortDescription: Arithmetic, algebra, geometry, statistics — with progressive reasoning.
mathematiques.longDescription: A complete pathway that follows the Quebec program's progression. Each concept is introduced with a concrete example, then practiced through progressive exercises, before being consolidated with open-ended problems.

p3p4: Read, write and compare numbers up to 100,000
Master addition and subtraction with regrouping
Discover simple fractions and decimal numbers
Measure lengths, areas and capacities in standard units
Recognize and classify common plane figures
p5p6: Compare fractions and convert them to decimals
Multiply and divide with large numbers
Calculate percentages and work with proportions
Construct geometric figures with instruments
Read and interpret bar and line charts
s1: Operate on positive and negative rational numbers
Calculate areas and volumes of common solids
s2: Solve first-degree equations with one variable
s3: Solve systems of two linear equations in two variables
Study affine and step functions
Use trigonometry in concrete contexts
Calculate equations of lines and circles
Analyze variance and mean deviation
s5: Master the logarithmic function and trigonometric identities
Work with vectors (depending on the sequence)
Solve linear optimization problems
Analyze statistical distributions
Prepare for the ministerial uniform exam

francais.title: French
francais.shortDescription: Reading, writing, grammar and oral communication.
francais.longDescription: An approach that favors fine-grained comprehension over rote memorization of rules. Exercises span genres (narrative, informative, argumentative) and feedback consistently explains the why rather than only the verdict.

p3p4: Read short texts aloud and silently
Enrich vocabulary through daily reading
Write complete, properly punctuated sentences
Master simple agreements (noun/adjective)
Conjugate common verbs in present, passé composé and future
p5p6: Read youth novels and identify the main idea
Write a structured narrative text
Master subject-verb agreement
Identify word classes in a sentence
Prepare and deliver an oral presentation to the class
s1: Read and analyze different narrative genres
Write a clear, structured explanatory text
s2: Study works from the French-speaking literary heritage
Produce a descriptive text rich in stylistic devices
Revise and improve a text based on criteria
Prepare an oral communication with visual support
s3: Analyze argumentative texts and identify their thesis
Write an opinion text supported by arguments
Master complex syntax and advanced punctuation
Study a novel by a Quebec or francophone author
Moderate a structured debate with several participants
s4: Analyze the narrative structure of a complete novel
Prepare an oral or written literary critique
s5: Produce a critical essay on a literary work
Study two long works for the uniform exam
Master renewed grammar and linguistic revision
Analyze 20th- and 21st-century literary texts
Prepare for the French writing uniform exam

anglais.title: English
anglais.shortDescription: Oral communication, reading and writing in second language.
skills: Reinvest understanding of texts read or heard
anglais.longDescription: A pathway centered on real communication rather than memorization. Activities alternate between listening comprehension (podcasts, videos), graded reading, guided and free writing, with concrete real-life scenarios.

p3p4: Recognize familiar vocabulary (family, school, colors)
Participate in simple oral interactions
Read aloud short illustrated texts
Write words and sentences with a model
Sing and recite rhymes in English
p5p6: Understand short messages on familiar topics
Answer open-ended questions orally and in writing
Read age-appropriate stories
Produce a short personal text with support
Discover anglophone culture through songs and films
s1: Read and understand short narrative texts
Produce a written text of several paragraphs
Listen to and summarize short audio content
s2: Argue simply orally and in writing
Master present, past and future tenses
s3: Read literary short stories and discuss them
Produce a structured written text (500+ words)
Deepen grammar (conditional, passive voice)
Analyze an audiovisual work
Carry out a multimedia communication project
s4: Master compound tenses and complex structures
s5: Analyze literary works and essays
Produce a developed argumentative or descriptive essay
Moderate a panel discussion or debate in English
Master language registers (formal, informal, academic)
Explore the cultures of the contemporary anglophone world

sciencesTechnologie.title: Science and technology
sciencesTechnologie.shortDescription: Natural sciences and technology, from Cycle 2 of primary through secondary.
skills: Explore the world of science and technology
Make use of tools, objects and processes
sciencesTechnologie.longDescription: A subject where hands-on investigation drives understanding. Activities start from a concrete question, propose an investigation, then invite generalization. Concepts are consistently tied back to everyday life.

p5p6: Observe and classify living things
Understand the water cycle and states of matter
Experiment with light, sound and heat
Study the solar system and Earth
Measure and use simple instruments
s1: Distinguish matter and energy (mass, volume, density)
Study the cell and classification of living things
s3: Study static and dynamic electricity
Understand genetics and reproduction
Analyze climate change
Distinguish acids, bases and salts
Carry out a complete technological project
s4: Prepare for the STE or SE ministerial exam
s5: Deepen physics (optics, electromagnetism)
Study organic chemistry and solutions
Analyze biotechnology
Carry out an autonomous research project
Connect science to societal issues

histoireQuebecCanada.title: History of Quebec and Canada
histoireQuebecCanada.shortDescription: From early societies to the present day, with a Quebec perspective.
skills: Examine social realities from a historical perspective
Interpret social realities using the historical method
histoireQuebecCanada.longDescription: A pathway that emphasizes reading of sources and connecting events. Exercises work on chronology, document analysis and historical writing, without falling into date-only memorization.

p3p4: Discover Iroquoian and Algonquian societies around 1500
Compare the ways of life of the Inuit and the Mi'kmaq
Place societies on a timeline
Study the organization of territory and communities
Read a historical map and extract information
p5p6: Study Canadian society around 1820 and 1905
Understand industrialization and immigration
Discover 20th-century Quebec society
Compare a democratic and a non-democratic society
Use age-appropriate primary sources
s3: Study the first occupants of Quebec territory
Analyze the emergence of a colonial society in New France
Understand political changes from 1760 to 1840
Interpret maps, engravings and period texts
Master the historical method (facts, interpretations, sources)
s4: Study the formation of the Canadian federal regime (1840–1896)
Understand the Quiet Revolution and its aftermath
Connect contemporary issues to their historical roots
Prepare for the uniform history of Quebec and Canada exam

geographie.title: Geography
skills: Read the organization of a territory
Build citizen awareness on a planetary scale
geographie.longDescription: A pathway that develops the ability to locate, compare and analyze territories. Exercises work on map reading, aerial-photo interpretation, and human and environmental issues, with a focus on Quebec and Canada.

p3p4: Read a map and use its elements (legend, scale, orientation)
Distinguish urban and rural landscapes
Locate Quebec and its administrative regions
Describe economic activities of the territory
Compare places using photographs
p5p6: Locate Canadian provinces and territories
Study regions of the world (Amazon, Arctic)
Analyze relationships between climate and landscape
Use digital geographic tools
Understand population movements
s1: Compare urban, rural and regional territories of Quebec
Analyze Indigenous territory and its issues
Formulate a territorial issue with a geographic question
s2: Study forest, energy and tourism territories
Analyze human impact on natural environments
Compare two territories on similar issues
Prepare for the rest of the social universe curriculum

educationFinanciere.title: Financial education
educationFinanciere.shortDescription: Budget, consumption, taxation and life projects.
skills: Take a position on a financial issue
Evaluate the consequences of a financial decision
educationFinanciere.longDescription: A mandatory Secondary 5 course that prepares students for adult life. Modules concretely address renting an apartment, negotiating a salary, reading a pay slip, comparing credit offers, opening an RRSP or TFSA, and filing a simple tax return.

s5: Build a realistic personal budget (income, expenses, unexpected items)
Compare credit and student loan offers
Understand the pay slip and the tax return
Analyze a life project (studies, housing, car) financially
Distinguish savings, investment and financial products (RRSP, TFSA)

educationPhysiqueSante.title: Physical education and health
educationPhysiqueSante.shortDescription: Varied physical activities, fitness and healthy habits.
skills: Perform movement skills in different physical activity settings
Interact with others in different physical activity settings
educationPhysiqueSante.longDescription: A pathway that focuses on regular practice and understanding your body. Theoretical sessions complement the practical classes: movement anatomy, training planning, sports nutrition, injury prevention, mental well-being.

Cooperate in team games

Recognize the effects of exercise on the body
Respect safety rules
p5p6: Participate in team sports
Evaluate your own physical condition

s2: Deepen team sports and their tactics
Plan meals according to energy needs
Address mental health and stress management
s3: Choose physical activities suited to your goals
Design a four-week training cycle
Analyze a nutrition label

s4: Discuss eating disorders and their warning signs
s5: Develop a long-term physical activity plan

cultureCitoyenneteQuebecoise.title: Quebec culture and citizenship
cultureCitoyenneteQuebecoise.shortDescription: Identity, diversity, democracy and culture in Quebec.
skills: Deliberate on ethical and cultural issues
Engage in dialogue in a pluralistic society
cultureCitoyenneteQuebecoise.longDescription: A course that replaced Ethics and Religious Culture as of 2023–2024. It addresses Quebec culture, democratic participation, applied ethics and living together, without religious instruction. Discussions rely on concrete cases and classroom scenarios.

p3p4: Discover rules of life at school and at home
Recognize differences and similarities between students
Understand everyone's roles and responsibilities
Identify emotions and ways to express them
Participate in collective classroom decisions
p5p6: Understand Quebec's symbols and institutions
Discuss your cultural affiliations
Recognize forms of discrimination and respond to them
Address relations between Indigenous peoples and the State
Exercise a concrete citizen role at school
s1: Analyze the influence of groups on individual choices
s2: Understand the role of media in public opinion
Analyze situations of inequality or exclusion
Practice respectful dialogue on sensitive topics
s3: Study secularism and the role of religion in society
Deepen ethics (consent, responsibility, justice)
Analyze Indigenous culture and francophone communities outside Quebec
Discuss digital issues (privacy, disinformation)
Build an argued position on a societal issue
s4: Understand social movements and their role
Study tensions between individual and collective rights
Participate in a community engagement project
s5: Deepen applied ethics (bioethics, environment, work)
Analyze citizen participation in a democracy
Explore Quebec culture in its artistic dimensions
Build a structured written and oral argument
Prepare for your role as an adult citizen

mondeContemporain.title: Contemporary world
mondeContemporain.shortDescription: Global issues of population, wealth, power and environment.
skills: Take a position on a contemporary world issue
mondeContemporain.longDescription: A mandatory Secondary 5 course that decodes international current events. Each topic is addressed through recent case studies (demographic transitions, climate change, wealth inequality, armed conflicts), with critical reading of media sources and argued positioning.

s5: Analyze demographic transitions (migration, aging)
Understand global environmental issues
Study wealth inequality between countries
Analyze armed conflicts and international interventions
Build an argument on a current global issue

primaire3.title: Grade 3
primaire3.shortDescription: First half of Cycle 2 in elementary school. Students consolidate reading, writing and early maths.
primaire3.longDescription: In Grade 3, students enter Cycle 2 of elementary school. The year focuses on fluent reading, first structured writing, and giving meaning to arithmetic operations. Social studies (history, geography, culture) progressively take their place.
goals: Read short texts fluently and with comprehension
Write complete sentences and short paragraphs
Observe and describe the surrounding world

primaire4.title: Grade 4
primaire4.shortDescription: End of Cycle 2 in elementary school. Students gain autonomy and structure their thinking.
primaire4.longDescription: In Grade 4, students complete Cycle 2. Focus shifts to longer written productions, multiplication and division, and a deeper exploration of Quebec and Canada.
goals: Locate themselves in time and space (Quebec, Canada)

primaire5.title: Grade 5
primaire5.shortDescription: Start of Cycle 3. Students learn to argue and to investigate.
primaire5.longDescription: Cycle 3 of elementary school raises the bar: reading to learn, writing to convince, reasoning to solve. Fractions, percentages and geometry take a central role in mathematics.
goals: Read to learn across all subjects
Work with fractions, decimals and percentages
Develop a research and verification method

primaire6.title: Grade 6
primaire6.shortDescription: Final year of elementary. Explicit preparation for secondary school.
primaire6.longDescription: Grade 6 closes Cycle 3. Students consolidate everything learned in elementary and prepare the transition to secondary: independent work, note-taking, more abstract problem solving and first digital competencies.
goals: Work in teams on subject-based projects
Prepare for the transition to secondary school

secondaire1.title: Secondary 1
secondaire1.shortDescription: Entry into secondary school. Students explore disciplines and develop work methods.
secondaire1.longDescription: Secondary 1 is a transition year — organisation by subject and by teacher. Students consolidate elementary learnings and begin algebra, world geography and experimental sciences.
goals: Organise work and manage an agenda

secondaire2.title: Secondary 2
secondaire2.shortDescription: End of Cycle 1 in secondary. Students deepen scientific and literary methods.
secondaire2.longDescription: Secondary 2 closes Cycle 1 with higher ambition: analysing texts, modelling in mathematics, distinguishing living from non-living in science. Geography officially ends this year.

secondaire3.title: Secondary 3
secondaire3.shortDescription: Start of Cycle 2 in secondary. Students begin Quebec history and prepare their path choices.
secondaire3.longDescription: Secondary 3 opens Cycle 2. It is the year when History of Quebec and Canada officially begins — a thread continued until the end of secondary. Students also start choosing options and mathematics sequences.
goals: Make informed choices for the next steps

secondaire4.title: Secondary 4
secondaire4.shortDescription: Pivotal year. End-of-cycle ministerial exams and CEGEP preparation.
secondaire4.longDescription: Secondary 4 is pivotal: students complete History of Quebec and Canada (1840 to today), take ministerial exams, and choose the mathematics sequence that will shape their CEGEP admission.
goals: Close History of Quebec and Canada (1840 →)
Choose and master the mathematics sequence

secondaire5.title: Secondary 5
secondaire5.shortDescription: Final year before CEGEP. Financial Education and Contemporary World complete the path.
secondaire5.longDescription: Secondary 5 is the final year of compulsory schooling in Quebec. Two subjects are introduced: Financial Education (budgeting, consumption, credit) and Contemporary World (power, wealth, population, tensions). Students end with the single French exam.
goals: Manage a budget, understand credit, save

faq.heroTitle: The questions that come up most often
faq.heroSubtitle: If you can't find your answer here, write to us — we respond to everything.

items.q1: What ages is EduQuiz designed for?
items.a1: EduQuiz covers Grade 3 through Secondary 5, with fine level adjustment within each subject. Younger learners may also benefit from specific domains.
items.q2: Is the tool aligned with the PFEQ?
items.a2: Yes. Pathways follow the Quebec school's training program. Objectives displayed before each chapter map to the corresponding disciplinary competencies.
items.a3: Data is hosted in Quebec, encrypted, never resold, and you can access, export or delete it at any time. See the Privacy page for details.
items.q4: Do I have to pay to start?
items.a4: No. The Discovery plan is permanently free and covers two subjects of your choice. You only move to a paid plan if you want to.
items.a5: The iOS and Android app arrives in Phase 2. The current web site is fully responsive and usable on phones.
items.q6: Can I create an account for my whole family?
items.a6: Yes. The Family+ plan supports up to 4 learner profiles under a single parent account, with individual reports and a consolidated dashboard.

privacy.heroSubtitle: What we collect, why, and how you can exercise your rights.
paragraphs: Solutions Infos inc., a Quebec company based in Montreal, operates EduQuiz and acts as data controller within the meaning of Quebec Law 25.
Data collection is limited to what is strictly necessary: account identifiers, exercise answers, progress, language preferences, technical logs.
Data is hosted in Quebec (Montreal), encrypted at rest and in transit. It is never sold or shared with commercial third parties.
Your rights: access, rectification, portability, deletion, withdrawal of consent. They can be exercised from the account Settings or by email to privacy@solutions-infos.quebec.
Retention: learning data is kept for 24 months after last activity then anonymized. Technical logs are kept for 90 days maximum.
Processors: hosting is provided by a vendor whose servers are located in Quebec. Transactional emails are sent by a Canadian provider. A complete list is available on request.

terms.heroSubtitle: The rules for using the service, in plain language.
paragraphs: By creating an EduQuiz account, you accept these terms. If you are acting on behalf of a minor student, you must be legally entitled to do so.
The service is provided as-is, intended to support learning. It is not a substitute for schooling or professional pedagogical advice.
An account is strictly personal. Sharing credentials between multiple people is forbidden; family plans exist precisely to cover multi-user usage.
You agree to use the service legally and respectfully: no offensive content, no attempt to bypass security, no automated scraping.
We may suspend an account in case of serious or repeated violations of these terms. Data remains available for export for 30 days after suspension.
Termination is possible at any time from the account area. Amounts already charged are not refunded pro rata, except as required by law.

cookies.heroSubtitle: Which cookies we use, what for, and how to refuse them.
paragraphs: EduQuiz uses a limited number of cookies, strictly necessary for the service to function or for its security. No advertising cookie, no third-party commercial tracker.
Strictly necessary cookies: authenticated session, CSRF protection, language preference. They do not require your consent because the service cannot function without them.
Analytics cookies: enabled only with your explicit consent. Statistics are aggregated and do not let us re-identify you personally.
You can change your preferences at any time in the account Settings or delete cookies from your browser. Refusing optional cookies does not affect service availability.
Retention: session cookies expire when the browser closes. Language preference cookies last 12 months. Analytics cookies last 13 months maximum (CAI standard).

accessibility.heroSubtitle: Our commitment so that everyone can learn with EduQuiz.
paragraphs: EduQuiz targets WCAG 2.1 Level AA conformance. Each page is audited before release and feedback from users with disabilities is prioritized.

Applied principles: sufficient contrast, adjustable text size without content loss, full keyboard navigation, text alternatives for all meaningful images, clear semantic structure (headings, lists, landmarks).
Known improvement areas: some progress charts do not yet provide exhaustive text alternatives. A remediation plan is in progress.
Reporting a problem: write to accessibility@solutions-infos.quebec describing the observed behavior, the page involved and your assistive tool. We respond within 5 business days.
Conformance: this statement is updated annually or after any significant product change.

loi25.heroSubtitle: How EduQuiz complies with the Act respecting the protection of personal information in the private sector, as modernized by Law 25.
paragraphs: Privacy officer: the person in charge within Solutions Infos inc. can be reached at privacy@solutions-infos.quebec.
Transparency: the privacy policy describes in plain language the data collected, the purposes, and any third parties involved. Substantial changes are notified by email and announced on this page.
Consent: any collection not strictly necessary to the service requires explicit, granular consent that can be withdrawn at any time without friction.
Minimization and retention: only data useful to the service is collected; it is kept only as long as strictly required, then anonymized or deleted.
Rights of individuals: access, rectification, portability, deletion, withdrawal of consent, de-indexing. Each request is processed within 30 days.
Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA): carried out before any significant product change. Documentation is available on request from partner schools.
Incident: in case of a breach likely to cause serious harm, notification to the Commission d'accès à l'information and to affected individuals as soon as reasonably possible.
